songs.name: It Must Have Been The Roses

ai_show_review.summary: Soaring Peggy‑O, tight Feel Like A Stranger chain & vibrant second‑set jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The Baltimore Civic Center show shines with a blistering second set that strings together Feel Like A Stranger → Franklin's Tower → Estimated Prophet → Terrapin Station flawlessly. Highlights include an inspired Peggy‑O solo, a soaring Stella Blue, and a tight Wheel → Truckin' transition. Overall the performance is high‑energy and well captured by several excellent mixes.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at Baltimore Civic Center on April 19, 1982 is a quintessential early‑80s Dead night that balances lyrical intimacy with big‑room propulsion. Jerry Garcia’s voice is crisp and his guitar work sings—most memorably on Peggy‑O where he launches into an extended, soaring solo that lifts the whole band. Phil Lesh anchors the marathon second‑set flow with deep, resonant bass lines that drive the Raven/Space improvisation and keep the Feel Like A Stranger → Franklin's Tower sequence in a tight groove. Brent Mydland’s keyboards add bright texture, especially during Estimated Prophet and Stella Blue, while Bob Weir contributes solid rhythm work and vocal harmonies throughout. The dual‑drum engine of Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann locks the rhythmic foundation, propelling the Wheel into Truckin' and onward through a jubilant Around & Around/Good Lovin' finale. Though some recordings note minor glitches on Terrapin Station, the best matrix blend captures the full dynamic range with clarity, making this show a must‑listen for fans of the band’s high‑energy period.

best_recording.reason: Matrix mix (≈60 % soundboard, 40 % audience) offers crisp, balanced audio with minimal glitches, preserving the full energy of the performance.

Raven/Space segment showcases deep bass work and exploratory improvisation

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers immaculate vocals and expressive guitar work, highlighted by a soaring solo on Peggy‑O and tight leads throughout the second‑set flow.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides deep, resonant bass that drives the extended jams, especially during Raven/Space and the seamless Feel Like A Stranger → Franklin's Tower sequence.
band_performance.Bob: Weir offers solid rhythm guitar and vocal harmonies, keeping the band grounded while adding texture on ballads and high‑gear moments alike.
band_performance.Brent: Mydland’s keyboards are bright and crisp, with standout touches on Estimated Prophet and Stella Blue; his solo work adds melodic depth to the jams.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart supplies dynamic percussion that enhances the spacey sections and keeps the groove rolling through the second set.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann locks in a steady, propulsive beat, driving the Wheel → Truckin' transition and maintaining momentum into Good Lovin'.
